paras.t: Tulit ergo rex annulum quo utebatur, non solum ad manus suæ ornatum, sed item ad litteras sigillandas, sicut tunc moris fuit. In annulis demum talibus fuit signum formatum ad imprimendum et signandum epistolas. De manu sua, et dedit eum Aman, ut juxta suum conceptum dictaret et sigillaret ex nomine regis litteras mortis contra Judæos. Credidit Assuerus nimis impio Aman, non inquirens accusationis veritatem. Facilitas autem credulitatis decipit multos, et in præsidentibus periculosa est subditis, etiam bonis.
paras.en: [[3:10|And the king took the ring that he used|Tulit ergo rex annulum quo utebatur]], not only to adorn his hand but also to seal letters, as was then the custom; for in such rings a device was cut for impressing and sealing letters. [[3:10|from his own hand, and gave it to Aman|De manu sua, et dedit eum Aman]], that he might dictate according to his own design, and seal in the king's name, letters of death against the Jews. Assuerus believed the most wicked Aman too readily, not inquiring into the truth of the accusation. Now readiness to believe deceives many, and in those who rule it is dangerous to their subjects, even to the good.

paras.t: Vocatique sunt scribæ, id est scriptores, regis. Scriba tamen frequenter accipitur pro sapiente seu doctore, vel legisperito.
paras.en: [[3:12|And the king's scribes were called|Vocatique sunt scribæ, id est scriptores, regis]]: *scribes*, that is, writers. Yet *scribe* is often taken for a wise man or teacher, or one learned in the law.

paras.t: Et litteræ missæ sunt per cursores regis ad universas provincias regni ejus, ut occiderent omnes Judæos a puero usque ad senem, id est universos, etiam infantulos atque decrepitos, et mulieres, id est cunctas personas feminei sexus. Et ut proniores essent gentiles hoc facere, dabatur facientibus illud licentia diripiendi ac retinendi bona Judæorum, quos trucidarent. Ideo subditur, et bona eorum diriperent. Sic quippe filii Israel vastaverunt Amalecitas: tamen contra præceptum Dei, pepercerunt pecoribus Amalec, sicut primo Regum fertur.
paras.en: [[3:12|and the letters|Et litteræ]] [[3:13|Were sent by the king's messengers to all provinces|missæ sunt per cursores regis ad universas provincias]] of his kingdom, [[3:13|to kill|ut occiderent]] [[3:13|all the Jews, both young and old|omnes Judæos a puero usque ad senem]], that is, all of them, even little infants and the decrepit, [[3:13|and women|et mulieres]], that is, all persons of the female sex. And that the gentiles might be the readier to do this, leave was given to those who did it to plunder and keep the goods of the Jews whom they slaughtered. Therefore it is added: [[3:13|and to make a spoil of their goods|et bona eorum diriperent]]. For so the children of Israel laid waste the Amalecites[[1 Kings 15:7||]]; yet, against the command of God, they spared the cattle of Amalec, as is told in the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 15:9||]].

paras.t: Statimque in Susis metropoli regni, pependit edictum: id est, ex dispositione Aman, appensum est decretum in scriptis de Judæorum interitu, ne rex suam revocaret sententiam, sicut nec eam de Vasthi abjectione revocare audebat. Hoc loco ponit Josephus formam epistolæ prætactæ ex nomine regis cunctis ejus provinciis missæ: quæ infra continetur. Rege et Aman celebrante convivium, tanquam rem communitati saluberrimam ordinassent, et cunctis Judæis qui in urbe Susis erant, flentibus: imo, ut Josephus scribit, etiam civitas turbabatur, utpote Judæis captivatis compatiens.
paras.en: [[3:15|And immediately the edict was hung up in Susan|Statimque in Susis metropoli regni, pependit edictum]], the capital of the kingdom: that is, by Aman's arrangement the decree concerning the destruction of the Jews was hung up in writing, lest the king should revoke his sentence, just as he did not dare to revoke the one on the casting off of Vasthi. At this place Josephus gives the form of the aforesaid letter sent in the king's name to all his provinces, which is contained further on[[Esth 13:1||]] [the margin reads "Esther xi, 1–7" as OCR'd; the letter is Esther 13:1–7]. [[3:15|the king and Aman feasting together|Rege et Aman celebrante convivium]], as though they had ordained something most wholesome for the community, [[3:15|and all the Jews that were in the city weeping|et cunctis Judæis qui in urbe Susis erant, flentibus]]: nay more, as Josephus writes, even the city was troubled, as having compassion on the Jews held captive.

4.title: Expositio capituli quarti: Quæ quum audisset Mardochæus, scidit vestimenta sua
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Now when Mardochai had heard these things, he rent his garments

paras.t: Refertur hic, qualiter Mardochæus Esther reginam induxit ad intercedendum coram rege pro liberatione plebis Judaicæ.
paras.en: Here it is told how Mardochai induced Queen Esther to intercede before the king for the deliverance of the Jewish people.

paras.t: Quæ quum audisset Mardochæus, scidit vestimenta sua, ut moris fuit Judæis, imo et quibusdam gentilibus, sicut in libro Job, ipse Job et amici ejus leguntur vestimenta sua scidisse, et indutus est sacco, id est aspera saccinaque veste, in signum contritionis, spargens cinerem capiti, ad humiliandum se coram Deo, quasi pulverem se recognoscens ac cinerem; et in platea mediæ civitatis voce magna clamabat, ostendens amaritudinem animi sui: præsertim quia pensabat se esse occasionem tanti periculi, ac desolationis dijudicationisque populi sui; et hoc ejulatu usque ad fores, id est januas, palatii gradiens. Non enim erat licitum, indutum sacco aulam regis intrare. Unde secundum Josephum, usque ad aulam pervenit, et ante ipsam stetit: quam cum tali habitu ingredi, fuit prohibitum, ne hujuscemodi vestis, aut sic vestitus, miserabilisque apparens, horrorem incuteret regi, aut ejus magnificentiæ derogaret. In omnibus quoque provinciis, oppidis ac locis, ad quæ crudele regis dogma, id est præfatum edictum quasi doctrinaliter et apparenter dictatum, pervenerat, planctus ingens erat apud Judæos, plurimis sacco et cinere pro strato utentibus, ad impetrandum auxilium Dei, juxta illud Jeremiæ: Accingere cilicio, conspergere cinere.
paras.en: [[4:1|Now when Mardochai had heard these things, he rent his garments|Quæ quum audisset Mardochæus, scidit vestimenta sua]], as was the custom of the Jews, and indeed of some Gentiles, as in the book of Job we read that Job himself[[Job 1:20||]] and his friends[[Job 2:12||]] rent their garments; [[4:1|and put on sackcloth|et indutus est sacco]], that is, a rough garment of sacking, in sign of contrition, [[4:1|strewing ashes on his head|spargens cinerem capiti]], to humble himself before God, acknowledging himself to be as dust and ashes; [[4:1|and he cried with a loud voice in the street in the midst of the city, shewing the anguish of his mind|et in platea mediæ civitatis voce magna clamabat, ostendens amaritudinem animi sui]], especially because he reckoned that he was the occasion of so great a danger, and of the desolation and condemnation of his people; [[4:2|And he came lamenting in this manner even to the gate|et hoc ejulatu usque ad fores]], that is, the doors, [[4:2|of the palace|palatii gradiens]]: [[4:2|for no one clothed with sackcloth might enter the king's court|Non enim erat licitum, indutum sacco aulam regis intrare]]. Hence according to Josephus he came as far as the court and stood before it; for it was forbidden to enter it in such a dress, lest such a garment, or a man so clad and looking so wretched, should strike the king with horror, or detract from his magnificence. [[4:3|And in all provinces, towns, and places, to which the king's cruel edict was come|In omnibus quoque provinciis, oppidis, ac locis, ad quæ crudele regis dogma pervenerat]] (*dogma*, that is, the aforesaid edict, dictated as it were by way of doctrine and for show), [[4:3|there was great mourning among the Jews|planctus ingens erat apud Judæos]], [[4:3|many using sackcloth and ashes for their bed|plurimis sacco et cinere pro strato utentibus]], to obtain the help of God, according to the word of Jeremias: [[Jer 6:26|Gird thee with sackcloth|Accingere cilicio]], [[Jer 6:26|and sprinkle thee with ashes|conspergere cinere]] [the margin's reference is misread; the words are those of Jer 6:26].

paras.t: Ingressæ sunt autem puellæ Esther et eunuchi, id est pedisequæ ejus, et cubicularii qui erant castrati. Et apparet quod isti secrete noverunt Mardochæum et Esther esse cognatos. Nuntiaveruntque ei. Quod audiens Esther, consternata est, id est, mœrore oppressa; et misit vestem Mardochæo, ut indueret eam, sicque honeste vestitus, aulam intraret; quam accipere noluit Mardochæus, quia nondum finitum fuit malum illud pœnale, propter quod evadendum, induerat saccum. Accitoque Athach eunucho præcepit ut iret ad Mardochæum, et disceret cur hoc faceret. Egressusque Athach, invenit eum in platea civitatis: qui indicavit per eunuchum ei, scilicet Esther reginæ, omnia quæ acciderant in hoc casu, ut intraret ad regem, et deprecaretur pro populo suo. De quo faciendo excusat se, quia edictum fuit, quod quicumque non vocatus ingrederetur atrium regis, mox moreretur, nisi rex auream virgam quam tenebat in manu, ad sic introeuntem extenderet pro signo clementiæ. Hinc addidit: Ego igitur quomodo ad regem intrare potero, quæ triginta diebus non sum vocata ad eum? Habuit enim extra et alia multa deliciarum suarum objecta: et Deus omnipotens devotæ reginæ providit de tali continentia et quiete.
paras.en: [[4:4|Then Esther's maids and her eunuchs went in|Ingressæ sunt autem puellæ Esther et eunuchi]], that is, her waiting women, and the chamberlains who were castrated. And it appears that these secretly knew that Mardochai and Esther were kinsfolk. [[4:4|and told her|Nuntiaveruntque ei]]. [[4:4|And when she heard it she was in a consternation|Quod audiens Esther, consternata est]], that is, she was overwhelmed with grief; [[4:4|and she sent a garment|et misit vestem]] to Mardochai, for him to put on, so that, decently clad, he might enter the court; [[4:4|but he would not receive it|quam accipere noluit]], Mardochai, because that penal evil, to escape which he had put on sackcloth, was not yet ended. [[4:5|And she called for Athach the eunuch|Accitoque Athach eunucho]], [[4:5|and she commanded him to go to Mardochai, and learn|præcepit ut iret ad Mardochæum, et disceret]] [[4:5|why he did this|cur hoc faceret]]. [[4:6|And Athach going out|Egressusque Athach]] found him [[4:6|in the street of the city|in platea civitatis]]; [[4:7|And Mardochai told him all that had happened|qui indicavit ei omnia quæ acciderant]] through the eunuch, namely to Queen Esther, in this matter, [[4:8|and admonish her to go in to the king, and to entreat him for her people|ut intraret ad regem, et deprecaretur pro populo suo]]. She excuses herself from doing this, because it was decreed that whoever entered the king's court without being called should die at once, unless the king held out to one so entering the golden rod [*virga*: the Douay-Rheims has “sceptre”] which he held in his hand, in token of clemency. Hence she added: [[4:11|How then can I go in to the king, who for these thirty days now have not been called unto him?|Ego igitur quomodo ad regem intrare potero, quæ triginta diebus non sum vocata ad eum?]] For he had besides many other objects of his pleasures; and almighty God provided such continence and quiet for the devout queen.

paras.t: Quod quum audisset Mardochæus, rursus mandavit Esther reginæ, solita auctoritate loquens ad eam increpatorie et audacter, certus quod ipsa virtuosa domina patienter, non indignanter acciperet, dicens: Ne putes quod animam tuam tantum liberes, quia in domo es regis pro cunctis Judæis, id est, noli putare quod a sententia mortis contra Judæos promulgata, præserves propriam vitam dumtaxat per hoc, quod facta es contubernalis et conjux regis, et ideo non cures pro populo tuo rogare. Si enim nunc silueris, non rogando regem pro tuis, per aliam occasionem liberabuntur Judæi, id est, Deus aliis modis ac viis, eis (ut spero) succurret: et tu et domus tua peribitis, id est, Deus justo judicio permittet te, et domesticos seu cognatos tuos occidi, eo quod neglexeris populo tuo in tanto periculo subvenire. Et quis novit, utrum idcirco ad regnum perveneris, id est, consors et contoralis regis effecta sis, ut in tali tempore parareris, id est, ut disponaris venire ad prætactam ruinam in tempore persecutionis istius, in quo deseris tuos? Vel sensus est: Quis novit, etc.? ac si dicat: Quamvis occulta sint Dei judicia, forsitan tamen idcirco imperatrix et regina facta es, quatenus ex præordinatione divina pares te succurrere nobis.
paras.en: [[4:12|And when Mardochai had heard this|Quod quum audisset Mardochæus]], [[4:13|He sent word to Esther again|rursus mandavit Esther]], the queen, speaking to her with his wonted authority, in reproof and boldly, sure that the virtuous lady would take it patiently, not indignantly, [[4:13|saying: Think not that thou mayst save thy life only, because thou art in the king's house, more than all the Jews|dicens: Ne putes quod animam tuam tantum liberes, quia in domo es regis pro cunctis Judæis]] [Denis reads *pro*, “for”, where the Vulgate has *præ*, “more than”], that is, do not think that thou wilt save thy own life only from the sentence of death proclaimed against the Jews by this, that thou hast been made the king's companion and wife, and so care not to plead for thy people. [[4:14|For if thou wilt now hold thy peace|Si enim nunc silueris]], by not asking the king for thy own, [[4:14|the Jews shall be delivered by some other occasion|per aliam occasionem liberabuntur Judæi]], that is, God will help them (as I hope) in other ways and by other means; [[4:14|and thou|et tu]] and thy house [Denis reads *domus tua*, “thy house”, for the Vulgate's *domus patris tui*] [[4:14|shall perish|peribitis]], that is, God by a just judgement will allow thee and thy household or kinsfolk to be killed, because thou hast neglected to help thy people in so great a danger. [[4:14|And who knoweth whether thou art not therefore come to the kingdom|Et quis novit, utrum idcirco ad regnum perveneris]], that is, hast been made the king's consort and bedfellow, [[4:14|that thou mightest be ready in such a time as this?|ut in tali tempore parareris]] that is, that thou mayest be disposed to come to the ruin spoken of in the time of this persecution, in which thou forsakest thy own? Or the sense is: Who knoweth, etc.? as if he said: Though the judgements of God are hidden, yet perhaps thou hast been made empress and queen for this, that by divine preordaining thou mightest prepare thyself to help us.

paras.t: Rursumque Esther Mardochæo mandavit: Congrega omnes Judæos utriusque sexus, et orate pro me, ut communitatis oratio mihi prosperum mereatur successum. Non comedatis et non bibatis tribus diebus et tribus noctibus, nisi eo modo quo jejunantes solent non manducare, videlicet solum semel in die: vel tam parce et sobrie comedatis in die, ut quasi nil reputetur: sicut de eo qui parum comedit, dicimus, Nihil manducavit. Et ego cum ancillis meis similiter jejunabo. Sicque ancillæ istæ videntur fuisse fideles, et forsan conversæ per suam reginam. Et tunc ingrediar ad regem, sperando quod Deus misericorditer mecum disponet, et mentem regis mihi propitiam exhibebit, contra legem faciens, intrando ad regem invocata, id est non vocata, tradens me morti, id est periculo mortis, pro liberatione populi mei, nisi Deus gratiose provideat et succurrat. Ivit itaque Mardochæus ad exsequendum reginæ præceptum.
paras.en: [[4:15|And again Esther sent to Mardochai|Rursumque Esther Mardochæo mandavit]]: [[4:16|and gather together all the Jews|Congrega omnes Judæos]] of both sexes, [[4:16|and pray ye for me|et orate pro me]], so that the prayer of the community may win me good success. [[4:16|Neither eat nor drink for three days and three nights|Non comedatis et non bibatis tribus diebus et tribus noctibus]], except in the way in which those who fast are wont not to eat, namely once only in the day; or eat so sparingly and soberly in the day that it may count as almost nothing, as we say of one who has eaten little: He has eaten nothing. [[4:16|and I with my handmaids will fast in like manner|Et ego cum ancillis meis similiter jejunabo]]. And so these handmaids seem to have been of the faith, and perhaps converted by their queen. [[4:16|and then I will go in to the king|Et tunc ingrediar ad regem]], hoping that God will deal mercifully with me, and will make the king's mind favourable to me, [[4:16|against the law|contra legem faciens]], by going in to the king [[4:16|not being called|invocata]], that is, uncalled, [[4:16|and expose myself to death|tradens me morti]], that is, to the danger of death, for the deliverance of my people, unless God graciously provides and helps. [[4:17|So Mardochai went|Ivit itaque Mardochæus]] to carry out the queen's command.
